observations: The changed line `return sum(values) / len(values)` divides by `len(values)`, which is 0 for an empty list, so `mean([])` raises ZeroDivisionError rather than returning 0.0 as the behavior_contract states.
The stated contract 'Empty input has mean 0.0 by this API contract' is not implemented anywhere in the supplied source; there is no guard for empty input.
Probe p1 `mean([])` is predicted to raise ZeroDivisionError (division by zero), contradicting the contract.
Probe p2 `mean([2, 4])` is predicted to return 2.0 (sum 6 divided by length 2), consistent with the contract for non-empty finite numeric lists.
No type validation exists; non-numeric or non-finite elements would propagate errors from `sum`, but the contract restricts input to finite numeric lists so this is out of scope.
static_findings is empty, so no tooling flagged the empty-input division; the defect is only observable via the contract comparison.
